facts.text: Patrick Henry, the famed American patriot, was born and raised in Hanover County, where his home Scotchtown still welcomes visitors.
The historic Hanover Courthouse, pictured on the county seal, served as the venue where Patrick Henry argued the Parson's Cause in 1763.
In 1953, the Barksdale Theatre opened at the Hanover Tavern, becoming the first professional theatre organization in central Virginia.
Hanover County’s name honors the Electorate of Hanover in Germany, reflecting King George I’s dual role as monarch of Britain and Elector of Hanover.
A local initiative highlights four pillars—history, outdoor recreation, agritourism, and events—to showcase the people, places, and experiences that define Hanover.
Hanover County sits within the Greater Richmond Region, blending rich colonial heritage with modern suburban life just north of the state capital.
